title: Walk Brevard to See White Squirrels & More!
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Take a walking tour of the city of Brevard. We will meet at 9:00. This walk will be 5 KM (3 miles).

Walk through picturesque neighborhoods, the grounds of a stately old mansion, a quaint park, and a vibrant downtown. End with a stroll through Brevard College, known for its music programs and small school atmosphere; the campus features a swift flowing stream and a fine clock tower. We often seen white squirrels scampering about; how many will you see?

This easy walk has some fairly gentle hills but is mostly on pavement. Dress for the weather. Tennis shoes should be fine; few will want walking poles. Be sure to bring water and a protein snack. Dogs are welcome. Strollers should be ok, with simple workarounds for the place or two where needed.

title: Forest Bathing: Flower Power!
description:
Forest Bathing: Flower Power!
with Asheville Wellness Tours 
Saturday, May 30  |  10 – 1pm 
REGISTER HERE 
Celebrate the ephemeral beauty of flowers during this immersive morning nature retreat! In Japan, the birthplace of forest bathing (Shinrin Yoku), they celebrate the annual cherry blossom bloom (Sakura) with a practice known as Hanami, which translates to “contemplate the flowers.” This experience gently invites us to cultivate our attention and sensory awareness, while noticing the evanescent nature of flowering, both within and around us. Together, we will explore our relationships with native wildflowers, ourselves, each-other, and the more-than-human-world. 
Your guide, Kelly Bruce, will lead you on a colorful journey through the blossoming spring forest, weaving mindfulness, breathwork, forest bathing and nature therapy together for a restorative morning on some of the trails less traveled at the North Carolina Arboretum. We’ll celebrate the experience in community, enjoying a wild-foraged tea ceremony and snacks. Bring an open mind and an open heart. All are welcome. Presented through Adult & Continuing Education Programs in collaboration with Asheville Wellness Tours. 
Kelly Bruce is a writer, forest therapy guide and nature connection mentor based in Hendersonville, North Carolina. Her mission is to help others deepen their connection with nature, community and Self. Kelly is an Association of Nature and Forest Therapy Certified Guide and Certification Consultant. She is Wilderness First Aid and CPR certified by the American Red Cross.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Plant Sale Class: Soil Amendments & Conditioners
description:
Plant Sale Class: Soil Amendments & Conditioners
with Phil Roudebush 
Saturday, May 30  |  11:30 am – 12:30 pm 
BREG – Elective 
REGISTER HERE 
What should we do to amend our heavy clay soils? Soil amendments include any material added and mixed into soil to improve the fertility, physical characteristics or beneficial microbial activity in the soil. Soil conditioners are amendments used to specifically improve soil structure. This class will discuss basic concepts of soil science and how soil amendments and conditioners can be used to improve soil health. 
Phil Roudebush is a native of Indiana and lived in Colorado, Missouri, Mississippi and Kansas before moving to North Carolina in 2015. He is a retired veterinarian who has worked in small animal practice, taught in several veterinary schools and did research, product development and technical communication in the animal health industry. Phil has maintained a large vegetable garden, herb garden, pumpkin patch, water garden and a 30-acre native grass hay pasture. He was an Extension Master Gardener in Shawnee County, Kansas before moving to Asheville and is a certified Extension Master Gardener Volunteer in Buncombe County.

title: Adult Studio: Landscape // Wild and Free
description:
Join instructor Ehren Fritz Gerhard in this three-hour session of plein air painting on location at Zealandia Estate! Students will interpret the landscape using a combination of abstract and realistic painting techniques. Learn how to utilize a limited color palette and limited brushes to emphasize the fundamental structure of your paintings. Minimalism in the landscape, expressive color palettes, bold brushstrokes, and visual contrast will be the primary focus of this session accompanied by instructor demonstration, guidance, and group critique. 
Ehren Fritz Gerhard completed his Master of Fine Arts from Arizona State University in 2013 and Bachelor of Arts from Florida Gulf Coast University in 2009.  He has been an Adjunct Professor of Drawing and Printmaking at Florida Gulf Coast University as well as Basic Design and Color Theory at Florida Southwestern State College. He lives in Asheville, North Carolina with his wife, daughter, son, and dog where he maintains an active studio, works on his garden and goes on primitive camping and fishing trips as often as possible.

title: SoulCollage® Open Studio
description:
Awakening Asheville
**SoulCollage®** is a playful and transformative method that helps us acknowledge all aspects of self. The process helps us discover our unique inner/outer guides and challengers in life. Together we will explore and express ourselves by making our own personalized deck, sharing cards, journaling, and consulting our cards about our own life questions. We will use simple tools—images, 5x8 cards, scissors, and glue, so no artistic experience needed!

Open Studio is a time when supplies and space will be available to create cards for your deck. You can drop in for a little while or stay the entire time. New and experienced practitioners welcome! While this is mainly time for independent creation, Michelle will be there to chat, answer questions, provide tips, and guide you through the process. If you’ve been curious about SoulCollage® this is a great way to get started.

Bring your water bottle and something to journal with. All other supplies will be provided.

**Materials Fee Contribution:** $5.00/Card

**About Your Guide:** I’m Michelle, an avid SoulCollage® Creatrix and lifelong educator who knows we are a network of connected humans. I believe we each have the capacity to improve our world by intentionally directing our individual and collective energies. I spend my time and energy expanding ideas, people, and communities that are lighting up the world with their precious energy. I’m excited to create with you!

title: shut in 10.5 mile cardio hike
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
meet/ park at the river park
WE HIKE AT A FAST PACE WITHOUT BREAKS. This is primarily a fitness oriented event. While we try to stay together as a group, we will not wait for extended periods at intersections. Sometimes a bit of trail running can even be involved. If you haven't hiked with this fitness group before and are unsure of your abilities, be prepared and know your way back to your car. If carpooling is involved please do so appropriately, or drive yourself to the trailhead.

HIKE DESCRIPTION:

Dogs Welcome. The hike is an out & back 10.5 mile LEVEL 7\* fitness hike that begins at the Bent Creek river park where we take a short connector trail to the MST (Mountain to Sea Trail) South, to the Sleepy Gap overlook, and back. The out hike has 3 steep climbs and for those who desire an additional climbing challenge, a spur trail of 400+ feet elevation is available that rejoins the regular MST trail at Sleepy Gap. The return has one steep climb with mild elevation changes between the 3 steeper downhill sections. The trail parallels the Blue Ridge Parkway and includes an overlook of the French Broad River valley and opposing mountains, distant views of Asheville. Bring water and snacks - we will stop at the turnaround point for a short break so Osa can have a snack (or three).

title: Pre-Event Picnic - Olivette Riverside Concert
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
*With warmer weather upon us, what could be better than a Sunday afternoon of connecting, socializing, and listening to great music with fellow Nomads at an outdoor concert by the beautiful French Broad River?*

**What:** Pre-Concert Social
**Where:** The Lawn - Olivette Riverside Pavilion
**Artists:** Caleb Caudle & the Sweet Critters
**When:** 3pm on Sunday, May 31st
**To Bring:** BYOB & BYOC (chair) + Sharable Snacks

**Details**
Join fellow music-loving Nomads for a pre-concert picnic on the lawn by the Olivette Riverside Pavilion. Use **[this link](https://www.chatthillsmusic.com/caleb-caudle)** to purchase tickets for **Caleb Caudle & the Sweet Critters** on Sunday, May 31st. Nomads attending the pre-concert gathering are invited to bring shareable snacks and appetizers, along with your beverages of choice.

This informal Nomads gathering starts at 3pm. Live music from Caleb Caudle & the Sweet Critters will be from 4 - 6pm.

**What to Bring**
Bring comfortable folding chairs and/or blankets for picnicking on the lawn. If you want to sit in the covered Pavilion for the concert, you will need your own chair.

**The Music**
No stranger to Asheville, **Caleb Caudle & the Sweet Critters** will be featured at Chatt Hills' 4th "**[Sundays by the River](https://www.chatthillsmusic.com/all-shows)**" concert series for 2026. Rooted in the North Carolina foothills and refined on stages across the world, Nashville-based **[Caleb Caudle](https://www.calebcaudle.com/)** delivers the kind of music that stays with you — soulful, honest, and impossible to put in a box. His sound weaves country tradition and indie spirit into something that feels both timeless and alive, drawing praise from the New York Times, Rolling Stone, and NPR, and earning him a spot on the hallowed stage of the Grand Ole Opry. Caudle's music is featured on Rolling Stone’s “10 New Country Artists You Need To Know” and “The 10 Best Country and Americana Songs To Hear Now” along with NPR’s “Songs We Love”. Whether you know him from Merlefest, Stagecoach, Kerrville or Sirius XM’s Outlaw Country, seeing Caudle live is a reminder of why music matters — raw storytelling, real emotion, and a voice that cuts straight through. Caudle's latest album, the 10-track "Heavy Thrill," is set for release on June 5. Come hear Caleb and the band for a riverside treat!

**Tickets**
We highly recommend purchasing your tickets in advance. Tickets are $25 each ($30.52, including fees) -- and kids are free! Well-behaved dogs are also welcome.

**[Tickets and more info](https://www.chatthillsmusic.com/caleb-caudle)**.

**Directions**
Olivette is just 15 minutes from downtown Asheville. Click **[this link](https://maps.app.goo.gl/rnqGwUiLLJghxo1r8)** to get directions directly to the parking area for the Pavilion. Otherwise, use the address below to get to Olivette and follow the Chatt Hills event signs to the Pavilion.
Carpooling is encouraged.

**Chatt Hills Music**
Chatt Hills Music is an independent non-profit organization dedicated to enriching communities through the power of live music. Chatt Hills brings an eclectic lineup of award-winning artists to Asheville and the surrounding region. From Americana and singer-songwriters to jazz, rock, and classical, every concert offers a unique musical experience.
This outdoor concert series takes place just minutes from downtown Asheville at the scenic Olivette Riverside Pavilion, located along the banks of the French Broad River—where great music meets beautiful views. World-class music, scenic views, affordable tickets — and kids are always free.

**The Venue**
Olivette is a 411-acre planned community and historic farm, located along the French Broad River, just 6.7 miles from downtown Asheville. An agrihood community, Olivette is home to a vibrant vegetable, fruit and flower farm. With 1.3 miles of river frontage, the community has a seven acre riverfront park with a pavilion, miles of walking trails, community gardens, a dog park, and multiple neighborhood gathering spaces.

description:

This is not traditional improvisation. Imagine Spirited Improv as a spiritual practice, where creativity meets consciousness and community. No experience necessary.

**ABOUT SPIRITED IMPROV**
Spirited Improv is a unique fusion of expressive arts, spiritual practice, and group play that helps you release fear, trust the unknown, and show up as your truest self.
Spirited Improv is a soul-centered community experience that uses improvisational play as the container for spiritual growth, personal transformation, and authentic connection. Rather than focusing on comedy or performance, we use improv as a living practice, one that invites presence, trust, curiosity, and responsiveness in the moment.

Facilitated by Jessica Chilton, who brings over 20 years of improvisational performing arts experience and 16 years as an expressive arts therapist, weaving creativity, spirituality, and presence into a safe, transformative group experience.

**2 HR COMMUNITY PLAYSHOP**
This special session takes place on the final day of the current Spirited Improv series, when we open the experience to the wider community.
You’ll join the participants who have been playing together throughout the series. You’re welcome to watch from the audience and enjoy the unfolding experience, or jump in and participate in the improvisational play alongside the group.
Great opportunity to try it out before joining a multi-week series.

**WHAT PAST PARTICIPANTS ARE SAYING**

“Spirited Improv is authentic, vulnerable and connective. It meets my need to deeply feel, be seen and see others. On my first night I experienced such a profound healing experience after sharing what was on my heart. It was like a sound, healing touch, full moon energy bath that opened my heart. ” \~ Kate

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

title: Wednesday night Bent Creek
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
Hard Times Trailhead near Lake Powhatan Rec Area
RSVP's don't open until 6PM Sunday night.
Weather: or not, I'll let you know if it's raining, and/or cancelled.
I did this hike series for many years before 2022, but I did it as a high-speed hike, and I am now doing it as a moderate speed hike. This is a numbers limited event and I expect people who sign-up to show up. Late cancellations, and those that don't show up are bumping other interested hikers, and they will not be allowed on future hikes.
If all goes well, I will try to post a hike most weeks, and for days Tue or Wed, distance, and start location, like switching between Hard Times trail-head and Bent Creek River Park, may change.
The current route is about 5.5 miles.
Please folks, this is intended as a moderate paced hike, and we'd like all attendees to keep up with the hike leader(s). This hike is intended as a workout hike for people to get in condition to do weekend hikes.
Moderate paced means 22-24 min miles, or 2 ½ mph.
As such, we do not take breaks, take in views, or snap photos along the way. Please make sure you're able to keep up with the group. This hike has always served as a good chance to get exercise during the week, meet new people, and create interest for weekend enjoyment hikes. It's a great introduction to the AHG family.
No need to RSVP "No" or "not attending" unless changing from a "Yes."
Please read the full description before RSVPing, and only sign up if you are sure you can go. Thanks in advance for keeping your RSVP up-to-date and not being a last-minute cancellation or no-show. This is an ongoing issue with Meetups and often keeps people on waitlists from being able to attend our hikes.
Hard Times Trailhead near Lake Powhatan Rec Area
Follow signs off of Brevard Rd (Rt 191) to Lake Powhatan Rec Area. The road is Bent Creek Ranch Rd. to Wesley Branch Rd. Follow signs to Lake Powhatan until you come to Hard Times Trailhead on your left, 2.5 miles. It is very clearly marked. Parking is very limited at the trailhead but there’s a paved pull-off just before the Hard Times trailhead and more parking just beyond at the Ledford Branch trailhead. We will access Bent Creek forest by way of Hard Times Trail and do some combination of loop and out and back.
Arrive at the trailhead BY 6:00. Because it is a weeknight hike, we are unable to wait for latecomers, fighting daylight.
\*\*\*If you are running behind, please post a comment on this Meetup page by 5:45 pm. There is no cell service at the parking lot, so if we don't have any advance notice of you running late by 5:45, we can't get any notifications at the trailhead and we will not wait for you.
We start the hike at 6:00, rarely do we get much later than that.
• Wear closed-toed footwear appropriate for hiking. The trail will consist of dirt, rocks, roots, mud and mulch.
• Bring plenty of water.
• Bring rain gear if a chance of rain is in the forecast.
Headlamps suggested
• Dogs on leashes the whole time are welcome. This is an active mountain bike area and it can get messy with dogs running loose among hikers and mountain bikers.
Please make sure to keep your RSVP up-to-date. You don't want to be "that person" who cancels last minute or no-shows and keeps someone from joining in if there's a waitlist. Thanks for your consideration - it is appreciated!
Feel free to post questions not covered in this description in the comments section.
Thanks - we'll see you on the trail!

RIGHT out of OLR parking lot

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Bonsai Update: Walking the Forest Meadow at the NC Arboretum
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
**Bonsai Update: The Bonsai in the Blue Ridge ticketed event will be going on June 4 – 7. You very well may want to stay after the walk for lunch and the Bonsai event. Plan accordingly.**

Meet inside the Baker Visitor Center at 09:30 a.m. Restrooms are available at the start point.

We will walk through the Formal Gardens and the Bonsai Exhibit. Then we will make our way to the Forest Meadow, walking around all the paths. We'll go down Running Cedar Road, across on Bent Creek Road (taking the Creekside Trails), and return on Wesley Branch Road.

Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. Some may want walking poles. Sneakers should be fine, unless it has rained recently. Be sure to bring plenty of water and a protein snack.

Dogs on leash are welcome, but are not allowed in buildings or the Bonsai Exhibit. Trail strollers should be ok.

The NC Arboretum does not have an admission fee, but they charge $20 per car parking fee (so pack as many people in your car as you can). We recommend for the driver to purchase the lowest level annual membership which includes free parking. (Of course, you may want a higher level membership, your choice.) We walk at the Arboretum at least six times per year.

title: Psychedelic Integration Circle
description:
Psychedelic Society of Asheville
Some experiences change us before we fully understand how. Through reflection, shared wisdom, and genuine community, this circle offers a safe and confidential space to make meaning of your experiences, and to let that meaning actually land in your life.

When we integrate with intention, we move through change with greater clarity, resilience, and compassion for ourselves and others.

We are delighted to welcome Becca Marshall as our circle holder. Becca is an Integrative Psychotherapist, Aligned Living Coach, Psychedelic Integration Guide, and founder of [ActivXchange](https://www.activxchange.com/) — Her work supports people navigating significant life transitions, entering adulthood, stepping into leadership, moving through healing and transformation, with grounded presence and genuine care.

This circle is open to anyone curious, those actively preparing for or integrating an experience, and those who have been walking this path for years. Our intention is simple: to foster connection, shared wisdom, and mutual support within our growing community here in Asheville. All are welcome.

A suggested donation of $10 helps cover venue costs and support future PSA offerings. No one will ever be turned away for lack of funds.

Please join [our Discord](https://discord.gg/XXqvXXsTkB) to stay more connected with our community, and feel free to stay tuned for more newsletter updates, as well.

We hope you're all enjoying a lovely Spring in Appalachia, and we very much look forward to being in circle with you in June! 💫

In psychedelic service,
The PSA Collective

description:
Asheville Introverts
\*UPDATE (Construction blockage) - We will be starting at **229 Riverside Dr.** and walking a path down Lyman street that takes us past Hi-Wire toward Amboy Road, and then turning back around.

* **Total Distance:** Approximately 3-4 miles (but your distance is your choice).
* **Time:** About 1.5 hours.
* **Flexibility:** Remember, this is your walk. If 3-4 miles feels like too much, you can turn around at any point (like when we reach Hi-Wire) to head back to the start.

We will meet at the location in the event picture.
Don't forget the suntan lotion if it's a sunny day :)
We will wait 10 minutes after the event time, and then we start the walk.

* **Pet Policy:** I am a huge dog lover myself (I have 3!) but to ensure the safety and comfort of every human in our group, I’ve decided to make these walks dog-free. Some members may have allergies or fears, and since I can’t predict how different dogs will interact with each other, I want to keep our environment as stress-free as possible. Thank you for understanding!

\*Please keep an eye on this meetup event for any updates if weather isn't ideal. If there is rain, we will probably reschedule.

title: Fantasy and Sci-Fi Silent Book Club
description:
Asheville Introverts
BOYB - Bring Your Own Book and rant or rave about your current Fantasy or Sci-fi titles! We will either be in the large room inside or out back on the patio depending on weather.

**What is a Silent Book Club?**
Referred to as "Introvert's Happy Hour", Silent Book clubs allow readers to engage with each other without the commitment of reading a shared title. Community members gather in the same place, have some casual chit chat, and then read silently together. **This group will focus on Fantasy and Sci-Fi titles (subgenres & related genres are welcome!)**

**How does it work?**
For the first 15-30 mins we will gather and engage in introductions. Feel free to discuss your recent favorites, mention a title that lives in your head rent free, or ask for recommendations! The best part of the Silent Book Club is being able to talk shop with other readers!

Once settled in we will dedicate 45 minutes to silent reading. Your book can be traditional, ebook, or audiobook. Read at your own pace!

Afterwards we will go around show-and-tell style and share what we read with the group. Feel free to share as much or as little as you want! Organic dialogue welcome!

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

No experience is required; we provide music, voice training and an enjoyable singing experience under expert leadership. description:
As a valued Museum Member, we invite you to join us for the exclusive reception of our newest exhibition, The Art of Paper: Selections of Handmade Paper Works from the Collections of Jordan D. Schnitzer and His Family Foundation 
4–5pm | Upper-Level Members 
Register Here 
5–7pm | All Members 
Register Here 
About the Exhibition
The Art of Paper: Selections of Handmade Paper Works from the Collections of Jordan D. Schnitzer and His Family Foundation | Curated by Brett Littman with Susan Gosin and Cynthia Nourse Thompson, the exhibition features 66 works by leading artists of the 20th and 21st centuries, including Helen Frankenthaler, James Rosenquist, Frank Stella, Jasper Johns, Mark Bradford, Glenn Ligon and others who have redefined handmade paper as an expressive artistic medium. The thoughtful selection of works chronicles the pioneering achievements within the discipline and reveals how the field of handmade paper art was a natural advancement of and response to the historic relationship between print and paper. Drawn exclusively from the renowned collections of Jordan D. Schnitzer and His Family Foundation, the exhibition highlights the inventive intersections of papermaking, printmaking and collaborative artistic practice.  
Please note:
Exhibition Previews are reserved for current Museum Members; please only register Members included in your membership. 
Join the fun—Become a Member today!

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Exhibition on Screen | Frida Kahlo
description:
Frida Kahlo is a phenomenon. She is arguably the world’s favourite female artist—beloved by young and old. Exhibition on Screen’s award-winning film—first released during covid to a restricted audience – is back by popular demand with an exciting new addition from the curators of the blockbuster transatlantic exhibition from Tate Modern and MFA Houston ‘Frida Kahlo: the Making of an Icon’. 
Who was Frida Kahlo? Everyone knows her face but who was the woman behind the bright colours, the big brows and the floral crowns? Take a journey through the life of a true icon, discover her art, and uncover the true story of her rebellious, passionate and turbulent life. 
Making use of the latest technology to deliver previously unimaginable quality, we take an in-depth look at key works throughout her career. Using letters Kahlo wrote to guide us, this definitive film reveals her deepest emotions and unlocks the secrets and symbolism contained within her art. 
Exhibition on Screen’s trademark combination of interviews with world experts and a detailed exploration of her art, with new special bonus footage from the curators of the blockbuster 2026 exhibition, delivers a treasure trove of colour and emotion. This personal and intimate film offers privileged access to her works, her home, her studio and highlights the source of her feverish creativity, her resilience and her unmatched lust for life, beauty and revolution. 
Created in close collaboration with world experts and those who knew her. Featuring additional new material from the curators of the groundbreaking new Tate Modern and MFA Houston exhibition. Directed by Ali Ray.

title: Summer Art Camp | Ancient to Modern: Mixed Media Traditions Reimagined (Rising 6th - 8th grade)
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
REGISTER HERE 
Throughout history, artists have experimented with wax, fabric, pigment, metal, and glass to create expressive and symbolic artworks. In this camp, we’ll explore how ancient art-making techniques like batik, encaustic, and gilded mosaics can inspire new creative directions. Students will work hands-on with traditional materials and reinterpret them through a contemporary lens, experimenting with resists, mixed-media layering, transparency, and texture.  
Meet the Instructor: Kristina Shriver
Kristina Shriver is a visual art educator with over 16 years of experience, working with students of all ages. She teaches at Asheville High School and serves as an AP Studio Art Reader and mentor for other art educators. Kristina designs hands-on, material-rich art experiences that connect historical techniques to contemporary practice, emphasizing experimentation, personal storytelling, and meaningful creative exploration.

title: Summer Art Camp | Appalachian Arts & Crafts (Rising 6th - 8th grade)
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
REGISTER HERE 
Blending creativity with cultural heritage, students will explore the artistic traditions of Appalachian culture through a series of hands-on crafts. They will begin the week creating vibrant painted barn quilts and learning basic weaving techniques with natural materials. They’ll spend the remainder of the week further developing their weaving skills to make reed baskets and needle felting a landscape.   
Meet the Instructor: Kati Robbins
Kati Robbins has over 12 years of experience as an art educator, teaching studio arts and crafts to a wide range of age groups in different learning environments. She is currently based in Asheville where she works as a high school art teacher. Her creative work focuses on mixed media and assemblage, with a strong interest in collaborative and community based projects. She is inspired by Appalachian craft traditions, natural materials and the surrounding landscape. When Kati isn’t teaching or making art, she enjoys gardening, cooking, reading and hiking in the mountains.

title: A Musical Evening with Decoda & Ringdown featuring Caroline Shaw & Danni Lee Parpan
description:
Decoda and Ringdown take the stage at the Asheville Art Museum for a vibrant, genre-defying evening of music. This special collaboration brings together Decoda, Carnegie Hall’s only affiliate ensemble, with Ringdown for an electrifying evening of chamber music. Featuring celebrated songwriter Danni Lee Parpan and Pulitzer-Prize winning composer and North Carolina native Caroline Shaw, Ringdown bridges classical and contemporary worlds together in a way that feels both expansive and deeply personal. 
This program features celebrated works of chamber music, alongside a collaborative set with Ringdown and Decoda, blurring the lines between classical, electronic, and indie pop. Kicking off the 2026 Decoda Chamber Music Festival, this concert experience is designed for devoted chamber music listeners and curious newcomers alike. 
————— 
Ringdown’s music is like calling your first love on a rotary telephone, percussively tearing out the hammers from a 1924 vintage upright, and flinging each of them into space while you wait for every heartache you’ve ever felt to quietly return. Collaborators Caroline Shaw and Danni Lee Parpan—who between the two of them have a Pulitzer Prize, a handful of Grammys, and a “Best Drum Major Award”—describe Ringdown as an electronic cinematic pop duo based in Portland, Oregon and New York City. Others have described Ringdown as the love child of Johannes Brahms and Brandi Carlile—if they were born in the same century and if Brahms was a queer woman. You decide. 
Decoda is an artist-led chamber music collective dedicated to creating a more compassionate and connected world through music. Decoda pairs virtuosic performance with deep community engagement, bringing chamber music to concert halls, schools, shelters, hospitals, and correctional facilities. 
Each summer in the Asheville region, Decoda leads the Decoda Chamber Music Festival, a dynamic training program for young musicians who seek to develop both artistic excellence and social impact. Through side-by-side performances, mentorship, and creative collaboration, participants explore how music can build community and inspire change.

description:
Every Third Thursday, the Museum comes alive with an evening filled with music, tours, art making, special cocktails in our rooftop café, and more! 
Enjoy live music from 5–5:45pm and 7-7:45pm with artists from the Decoda Chamber Music Festival, featuring festival ensembles Hashi Duo and The Varick Trio. 
————— 
Each summer in the Asheville region, Decoda leads the Decoda Chamber Music Festival (DCMF), a dynamic program that brings together emerging musicians for an immersive experience in performance, mentorship, and creative collaboration—exploring how music can build community and inspire change. 
Hashi Duo, Costa Rican classical guitarist Adrian Montero and Japanese pianist Moe Takamatsu, takes its name from the Japanese word for “bridge.” Their program creates a musical connection between Japan and Latin America, weaving together traditional and contemporary works in a vibrant cross-cultural dialogue. 
The Varick Trio features Kevin Kyaw (piano), Da Young (Rachel) Lim (violin), and Guilherme Batalha (clarinet), bringing together a rich blend of textures and voices in an engaging chamber music performance.

title: Curator's Talk | The Art of Paper
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join us as Susan Gosin and Cynthia Nourse Thompson, two of the three curators of The Art of Paper, will discuss the fascinating realization of this exhibition, which features works by acclaimed artists from the 20th and 21st centuries drawn from the extensive collection of Jordan D. Schnitzer and his Family Foundation.  
Highlights include the evolution of handmade paper art as a progression from and response to the historic relationship between print and paper, revealing another important story about the act of collaboration among artists, fine printers, and hand papermakers at renowned publishing studios.  
Susan Gosin grew up as a member of five generations of commercial papermakers in Wisconsin. After receiving her MFA at the University of Wisconsin, Madison, she cofounded Dieu Donné in New York City in 1976. She has been involved in the field of hand papermaking as an artist, educator, writer, lecturer, and collaborator for fifty years. Her work has been exhibited and collected by institutions such as MoMA, New York; the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York; and the Getty, Los Angeles.   
Cynthia Nourse Thompson is currently Professor and Director of Curatorial Affairs at the Zuckerman Museum of Art at Kennesaw State University. Prior to this position, for six years she was Associate Professor and Director of the graduate programs in Book Arts & Printmaking and Studio Art at University of the Arts in Philadelphia, PA, while also serving as curator for the Joy Pratt Markham Gallery at the Walton Arts Center in Fayetteville, AR. As a curator, Thompson has organized and curated more than 50 exhibitions since 2000. 
Arturo Herrera, Mine, 2007, pigmented abaca watermark on pigmented cotton base sheet with hand-cut collaged
pulp painting, edition 9/23, 60 x 30 inches. © Arturo Herrera, Collection of Jordan D. Schnitzer.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Othello by Montford Players
description:
Asheville Introverts
Passion, jealousy, and deceit take center stage in one of Shakespeare’s most gripping plays. Othello, a brilliant general, secretly marries Desdemona, but their happiness fuels envy in his cunning ensign, Iago. With whispered lies and clever manipulation, Iago turns love into doubt and trust into turmoil. Set against the vibrant worlds of Venice and Cyprus, this tale of love and betrayal explores how even the strongest hearts can be undone by rumor. Bold, emotional, and timeless, Othello keeps audiences on edge until the final curtain.

The show begins at 7:30pm.
Stepped ground seating is free, remember to bring blankets, pillows, campchairs, etc to be more comfortable. If you’d like to make an online donation before the show you can do so here: [https://www.montfordparkplayers.org/](https://www.montfordparkplayers.org/get-tickets-2/)

The actors will come around at intermission for cash or venmo donations and they typically have a food and drink vendor of some kind.

Asheville’s Montford Park Players is North Carolina’s longest running Shakespeare theatre company dedicated to providing exceptional dramatic entertainment for the enrichment, education, and enjoyment of their audiences, free of charge.

title: A Day of Music & Art
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join us for a vibrant Day of Art + Music with Decoda and artists from the Decoda Chamber Music Festival (DCMF). This all-ages experience invites you to explore the museum through sound, creativity, and connection.  
Enjoy an interactive performance with Decoda artists, take part in hands-on workshops that blend listening, composing, and visual art-making, and wander the galleries on a self-guided musical tour—where works of art are paired with live performances by DCMF musicians. The day culminates in Arboretum in the Museum, an immersive musical experience in which solo performances unfold simultaneously throughout the space, transforming the museum into a living, breathing soundscape. 
Schedule 
Noon–12:30pm — Live Music on the Plaza 
12:30–1:15pm — Interactive Performance (Decoda Artists) 
1:30–2pm — Creative Art & Music Making & Live Music on the Plaza 
2–2:45pm — Musical Gallery Tour 
2:45–3:15pm — Creative Art & Music Making 
3:30pm — Arboretum in the Museum 
————— 
Decoda is an artist-led chamber music collective dedicated to creating a more compassionate and connected world through music. As Carnegie Hall’s only affiliate ensemble, Decoda pairs virtuosic performance with deep community engagement, bringing chamber music to concert halls, schools, shelters, hospitals, and correctional facilities. 
Each summer in the Asheville region, Decoda leads the Decoda Chamber Music Festival, a dynamic training program for young musicians who seek to develop both artistic excellence and social impact. Through side-by-side performances, mentorship, and creative collaboration, participants explore how music can build community and inspire change. 
Free with Admission RESERVE TICKETS NOW

title: Mindful Meet & Mingle- Open to all Singles
description:
Mindful Meet & Mingle – Asheville Singles
Mindful Meet & Mingle
An evening of connection, conversation, and conscious community.

**This event is non secular and not affiliated with the event located in any way**.

Join us for a relaxed and welcoming gathering where mindful singles come together.

This isn’t speed dating or small talk, it’s about slowing down, being present, and meeting like-hearted people in a grounded, authentic space. Whether you're new to the area, exploring dating with fresh eyes, or simply looking to expand your social circle with conscious connections, this event is for you.

We'll begin with casual introductions, followed by lightly facilitated conversation prompts to spark deeper, more meaningful exchanges. Come solo or bring a friend—everyone will have a chance to connect in a low-pressure, friendly atmosphere.

What to expect:
\- Like\-minded singles open to mindful connection
\- Guided conversation starters to go beyond surface\-level chat
\- A chance to relax and be yourself

Whether romance blooms or you walk away with new friends and insights, this is an evening to nourish your social and emotional well-being.

Open to singles of all genders and orientations

Dancing on the Summer Solstice...

David Starfire
Headline for the Summer Solstice Dance, David Starfire, is known as the pioneer of the Global Bass genre and composer of music for meditation and psychedelic assisted therapy. Billboard summed it up best: "David Starfire brings a unique perspective to EDM."
David's Ascend album reached #7 on the iTunes World Music chart and he had two #1 remixes on Hype Machine. He's traded remixes with CloZee, Desert Dwellers, iLL Gates, Beats Antique, and SOOHAN.
David has performed at prominent festivals such as Winter Music Conference, Coachella, Outside Lands, Envision, Burning Man, Eclipse, and Lightning in a Bottle.

DJ Osiah
An ecstatic dancer turned DJ with a deep love for crafting ecstatic dance medicine journeys that break through the limiting ideas as to what “spiritual” is supposed to look and sound like. His mixes don't play by the rules. They are deep, bass-rich, soul-expanding, multi-genre, feeling-inducing meditations bringing in a full spectrum of e-motions that synchronistically match the vibe-sense context of the present moment at hand.

The StarTribe Vision
At StarTribe, we treasure finding solace in the company of kindred spirits, sharing love, joy, and the magic of dance.
It's unanimous: StarTribe dances are where the human spirit shines bright. (We don't call ourselves StarTribe for nothin'!)
Togetherness is the spirit of StarTribe, and you are warmly invited.

title: Father's Day Walk of the Western End of Maggie Valley
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Meet at Maggie Methodist, 4192 Soco Rd., Maggie Valley 28751, in the corner of the parking lot closest to Soco Rd., but furthest from the church building. We will meet at 2:00 p.m. There are no restrooms at the start point, so take care of any needs before you arrive.

The walk is pretty flat. Tennis shoes are fine; walking poles aren't needed. Dress appropriately for the weather. Bring lots of water and a protein snack. Dogs are welcome. Strollers are fine.

We will walk west on Soco Road to Fie Top, with one or two side excursions. We will cross Soco Road and then walk east on the opposite side of Soco Road as far as Town Hall. We will cross the road and head west again, finally returning to the Start Point.

Sights along the way include Mary Rathbone Rich Park, Tube World, and Joey's Pancake House.

This is a short, easy walk, about 3 miles, mostly on pavement. Hope to see you there!

title: Summer Art Camp | Art Around the World (Rising 3rd – 5th grade)
description:
JOIN THE WAITLIST 
Students will investigate artists and artworks from each continent using a variety of processes and materials. They will explore drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture and collage. During art camp, students will collect artworks to create a portfolio that crosses all continents and cultures from around the world.     
Meet the Instructor: Sarah Medsker
Sarah Medsker has a master’s degree in education and is an art teacher in western North Carolina, having taught students between kindergarten and 8th grade. Teaching children is her passion, as she has been facilitating art-making for over 15 years. When she is not teaching art, she loves traveling, cooking, reading and exploring professional development opportunities in the field of art education.

title: Summer Art Camp | Paper and Book Making (Rising 3rd – 5th grade)
description:
JOIN THE WAITLIST 
 The first two days of this camp will be about tearing up, mashing, blending and laying out paper to dry into curated sheets – cut and folded into books we will make on the following three days.  There are so many ways to make a book! Picture journals with ribbons, folded snake books and bedazzled covers!  
Meet the Instructor: Maggie Imhoff
Maggie Imhoff is an educator of twenty-three years, including, most recently, the Art teacher at Ira B Jones elementary school in Asheville, NC. She has taught at several summer camps, created outdoor art experiences for kids as well as directed at a children’s circus. She loves to celebrate art in her everyday life. She knits, paints, sings, and dances.  This quote from Phylicia Rashad sums it up: “Before a child speaks, it sings.  Before they write, they paint. As soon as they stand, they dance. Art is the basis of human expression.” As an art educator, it brings her joy to bring art to children’s lives.

title: Code with Asheville Monthly Meeting
description:
Asheville Tech Events
Are you curious or even passionate about using advocacy, technology and sensible design to create more equitable social and civic structures in Western North Carolina?

Whether you call yourself an organizer, a technologist, a designer, planner, concerned resident, all of the above or something else entirely, we want to be in relationship and build community together with you.
Check out a list of our current projects: [https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects](https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects)

What to expect:
Since project work takes place asynchronously—individually and in smaller squads—the goals of our monthly gatherings are to:

* build relationships and learn about each other's skills, interests and goals,
* learn what we are doing across the organization (project updates),
* provide opportunities to get involved with and/or initiate projects, and
* shape where we are going as an organization, co-creating the culture and course of our work together.

In this meeting, we will:

* gather virtually using Google Meet for group video chat,
* do brief introductions, with a prompt,
* share updates about the projects that we're working on, highlighting deliverables for the next month and areas where additional resources would be useful, and
* discuss proposals and new opportunities to engage with local government and community organizations.

It isn't all glamorous, but the stakes are low for showing up and we'd be delighted to join together with you in this work.

**Disclaimer: In all efforts to keep this Meetup a safe space, we all agree to keep anything said within the group private and confidential.**

Do you want to take your remote working game to the next level? Do you find yourself saying wtf is Manifesting Self??

Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: The Foundation

All of life comes to me with ease, joy and glory™

You will be given a whole toolbox that will allow you to break apart the foundation of limitation that we so often function from and build a new foundation, one of limitless possibility so that you can begin to create the life you truly desire.

Everything can change.

The question is, will you choose it?

title: Book + Art | Glorious Country: Frederic Church and the Celebration of the American Landscape
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
In this richly illustrated talk, Pulitzer Prize and National Book Award finalist Victoria Johnson shares the dramatic and consequential life of the artist Frederic Church (1826–1900), whose footsteps she followed around the globe for her “absorbing” (Ron Chernow) and “superb” (Publishers Weekly) new biography of Church, Glorious Country. Church’s curiosity, bravery, and passion for nature drove him to explore the world, but it was his astonishing talent that allowed him to bring the world to America at a time when landscape photography was in its infancy and most of his fellow Americans would never see a different country or continent. Among Church’s many destinations was Western North Carolina, where he painted along the French Broad River. Exhibited to acclaim abroad, Church’s blockbuster paintings persuaded skeptical European critics that the New World could, in fact, give birth to towering artists and furnish the subject matter for great art. At Olana, Church’s estate on the Hudson River, he forged an enduring masterpiece of architectural, interior, and landscape design. A master artist and citizen, Church brought the world to America, and America to the world. 
Presented in Frederic Church’s bicentennial year. 
About the Speaker
Victoria Johnson is the author of three books, including the Pulitzer Prize and National Book Award finalist American Eden: David Hosack, Botany, and Medicine in the Garden of the Early Republic. She holds a doctorate in sociology from Columbia University and an undergraduate degree in philosophy from Yale. She is Professor of Urban Policy and Planning at Hunter College of the City University of New York.

title: Exhibition on Screen | Frida Kahlo
description:
Frida Kahlo is a phenomenon. She is arguably the world’s favourite female artist—beloved by young and old. Exhibition on Screen’s award-winning film—first released during covid to a restricted audience – is back by popular demand with an exciting new addition from the curators of the blockbuster transatlantic exhibition from Tate Modern and MFA Houston ‘Frida Kahlo: the Making of an Icon’. 
Who was Frida Kahlo? Everyone knows her face but who was the woman behind the bright colours, the big brows and the floral crowns? Take a journey through the life of a true icon, discover her art, and uncover the true story of her rebellious, passionate and turbulent life. 
Making use of the latest technology to deliver previously unimaginable quality, we take an in-depth look at key works throughout her career. Using letters Kahlo wrote to guide us, this definitive film reveals her deepest emotions and unlocks the secrets and symbolism contained within her art. 
Exhibition on Screen’s trademark combination of interviews with world experts and a detailed exploration of her art, with new special bonus footage from the curators of the blockbuster 2026 exhibition, delivers a treasure trove of colour and emotion. This personal and intimate film offers privileged access to her works, her home, her studio and highlights the source of her feverish creativity, her resilience and her unmatched lust for life, beauty and revolution. 
Created in close collaboration with world experts and those who knew her. Featuring additional new material from the curators of the groundbreaking new Tate Modern and MFA Houston exhibition. Directed by Ali Ray. 
Purchase Tickets

location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
JOIN THE WAITLIST 
Discover the importance of illustrations in a variety of storybooks then create art in the style of each illustrator.  We’ll use a wide range of art mediums for each project as well as create a book of your own!  
Meet the Instructor: M Rathsack
M Rathsack, owner and instructor at M’s School of Art, has taught many mediums in many locations for all ages in Western North Carolina since 2006. She creates her own art as the Dancing Potter working primarily as a decorative raku potter.

title: Summer Art Camp | The Joy of Painting! (Rising K - 2nd grade)
description:
JOIN THE WAITLIST 
 In this camp, participants will explore different paint mediums and techniques.  We will work with watercolor, acrylics and tempera (all washable).  We will learn about brush techniques, finger painting, wax resist and printing to name just a few.  The color wheel, warm and cool colors plus complementary colors will be discussed and an avenue to explore. Your child will get lost in the engaging and colorful world of paint!  
Meet the Instructor: Maggie Imhoff
Maggie Imhoff is an educator of twenty-three years, including, most recently, the Art teacher at Ira B Jones elementary school in Asheville, NC. She has taught at several summer camps, created outdoor art experiences for kids as well as directed at a children’s circus. She loves to celebrate art in her everyday life. She knits, paints, sings, and dances.  This quote from Phylicia Rashad sums it up: “Before a child speaks, it sings.  Before they write, they paint. As soon as they stand, they dance. Art is the basis of human expression.” As an art educator, it brings her joy to bring art to children’s lives.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Historic Columbia SC Morning Walk—Governor's Mansion, Finlay Park, and More!
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Meet at 10:00 a.m. in the lobby of the Hampton Inn, 822 Gervais Street, Columbia 29223 (enter the lobby from the Lincoln Street side). Restrooms are available at the start point.

The trail takes you past the Woodrow Wilson Boyhood Home, around the Governor's Mansion, through the newly reopened Finlay Park, and through Memorial Park.

There are some moderate hills and stair climbing, but it is almost entirely on pavement. Tennis shoes are fine; some may want walking sticks or hiking boots.

Dress for the weather. It will likely be very hot. A hat and sunscreen are highly recommended.

**Plenty of water** and a protein snack are advised as always. Wheelchairs are not recommended, although strollers ought to be ok. Dogs are welcome.

Our Meetup group offers some version of this walk every three months. It's that good! You will surely enjoy it.

Traditionally, many of us eat at Five Guys (near the start point) after the walk. There are lots of other restaurants nearby. Give yourself plenty of time to enjoy your meal after you join the group for the walk.

title: Walk Waynesville from Mast General to Auburn Park & Green Hill Cemetery & Back
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Meet at 2:00 in front of the shoe department entrance to Mast General Store, 63 N. Main St., Waynesville NC 28786. The walk goes down Main Street, through the Auburn Park neighborhood, twice around Green Hill Cemetery, past the Shelton House Museum and HART Theater, and back to the start point.

There are some hills, so some may want a walking pole; sneakers should be fine. Dogs are welcome. Strollers should be ok. Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dress appropriately for the weather.

Parking is easier a block to either side of Main Street. Mast General Store doesn't have a public restroom, but we can direct you to one nearby should you need it.

title: AVL Digital Nomads - Book Club!
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**July Meeting - Book Swap & Planning!**

* Bring books that you would like to swap with other book club participants.
* We encourage active participation in choosing our reading material. Bring your book suggestions for planning. We’ll plan out the next 6 months of selections.

**Welcome** to our robust and engaging Book Club! We're a small, friendly group dedicated to fostering lively discussions about our monthly book selections. Whether you've read the entire book, just a few chapters, or even if you're simply curious about the title, we'd love to have you join us!

**Meeting Schedule**: We gather on the First Tuesday of every month for our book discussions.

What sets us apart is our small group size and directed discussions. This intimate setting allows for deeper, more engaging conversations where everyone's voice can be heard. It's the perfect environment for those who love to dive deep into themes, characters, and the intricacies of storytelling.

So whether you're a seasoned bookworm or just dipping your toes into the world of literature, we invite you to join us. Let's explore new worlds, challenge our perspectives, and forge new friendships - one book at a time!

**August Pick: *TBD***

description:

No experience is required; we provide music, voice training and an enjoyable singing experience under expert leadership. Our repertoire of music is fun and spans many styles - most songs are easy to learn and sing. Learning materials are provided to help you get started, and you will be paired with a singing "Buddy" so you can join in right away.

We will be here to greet you as early as 6:15pm to help you get situated.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Drupal Camp Asheville 2026
description:
Asheville Tech Events
Drupal Camp Asheville is an annual two-day conference that focuses on hands-on training and knowledge sharing for all levels of Drupal experience, with a bonus community day spent together in nature.

Drupal is a popular free open-source modular framework and content management system (CMS). It is used to build everything from personal blogs to enterprise applications. Millions of businesses, government agencies, and nonprofit organizations use Drupal because it is free and flexible. It is constantly being improved by the hundreds of thousands of dedicated developers that are part of the global Drupal Community.

The size of our camp is perfect for being able to access session speakers and even do your first session presentation. We are a welcoming event for people at all levels of Drupal knowledge and experience. Come learn and share in an awesome, laid-back environment.

Find all of the info about programming and tickets at https://www.drupalasheville.com.
